pharm: Vitamin D analogue that, after activation, regulates calcium and phosphate homeostasis and bone mineralisation
quick: Maintenance 600-800 IU/day; deficiency 50,000 IU weekly x6-8 weeks
Take with a meal containing fat to aid absorption
Recommended within RDA (600 IU/day); avoid excessive doses
Compatible; 600 IU/day RDA; higher maternal doses raise infant intake
Caution in impairment; active forms may be needed; monitor calcium
No specific interaction at normal doses
summary: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is a fat-soluble vitamin used to prevent and treat vitamin D deficiency and to support bone health, often with calcium. It is hydroxylated in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D and in the kidney to active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol), which promotes intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption and bone mineralisation. Excessive intake causes hypercalcaemia.
indications: Prevention and treatment of vitamin D deficiency
Dietary supplementation to support bone health and calcium homeostasis
Adjunct in management of osteoporosis and rickets/osteomalacia (with calcium)

dosage.d: 50,000 IU once weekly for 6-8 weeks, then 800-2000 IU/day maintenance

dosage.n: Higher therapeutic doses for documented deficiency

admin: Take with a meal containing fat to optimise absorption
Swallow capsules/tablets whole; oral drops may be placed on food or in liquid
High-dose weekly regimens should be supervised and monitored
Do not exceed recommended doses without medical advice
moa: Cholecalciferol is hydroxylated in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 and then in the kidney to the active hormone 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (calcitriol). Calcitriol binds the vitamin D receptor to increase intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate, promote bone mineralisation and modulate parathyroid hormone, maintaining calcium-phosphate homeostasis.

relative: Sarcoidosis or other granulomatous disease (increased sensitivity)

preg: Vitamin D within the recommended dietary allowance (600 IU/day) is recommended in pregnancy; deficiency should be corrected. Avoid excessive doses, which can cause maternal and fetal hypercalcaemia.
lact: Vitamin D is present in breast milk in amounts related to maternal status; the RDA in lactation is 600 IU/day. Standard supplementation is compatible; very high maternal doses increase infant intake and require monitoring.
renal: In renal impairment, conversion to active calcitriol may be reduced and an activated vitamin D analogue may be required; monitor calcium, phosphate and PTH. Use cautiously to avoid hypercalcaemia.
hepatic: Severe hepatic disease can impair 25-hydroxylation and reduce activation; use with caution and monitor vitamin D status.

moderate: Thiazide diuretics - increased risk of hypercalcaemia
Digoxin - hypercalcaemia may precipitate digoxin toxicity/arrhythmia
Other vitamin D analogues / high-dose calcium - additive hypercalcaemia
minor: Cholestyramine, orlistat, mineral oil - reduced vitamin D absorption
Phenytoin, phenobarbital, rifampin - increased vitamin D catabolism (higher requirement)
interactions.food: Take with a fat-containing meal to improve absorption
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction at usual supplement doses
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum 25(OH)D and calcium; high doses can raise serum calcium

common: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses
emergency: Severe hypercalcaemia (confusion, arrhythmia, renal failure) from gross overdose

monitoring: Serum calcium and phosphate (deficiency or high-dose therapy)
Renal function and urinary calcium with prolonged high doses
counsel: Take with a meal containing some fat for best absorption
Do not take more than recommended - too much vitamin D is harmful
Combine with adequate calcium and weight-bearing activity for bone health
Tell your doctor if you have kidney stones, high calcium or sarcoidosis
Report symptoms of high calcium (nausea, excessive thirst, confusion)
pk: Serum 25(OH)D rises over days to weeks after dosing
Stored in adipose tissue; effect persists for weeks
Store at room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Cholecalciferol (D3) is the reference vitamin D form for supplementation
Fat-soluble - take with food; stored in fat with a long half-life
Renal/hepatic disease may need activated analogues (calcitriol)
Monitor 25(OH)D and calcium when treating deficiency
missed: If a daily dose is missed, take it when remembered; if nearly time for the next dose, skip it. For weekly high-dose regimens, take the missed dose when remembered and resume the schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Excessive intake causes vitamin D toxicity with hypercalcaemia: nausea, vomiting, weakness, polyuria, polydipsia, confusion, and with chronic overdose nephrocalcinosis and renal impairment. Stop vitamin D and calcium, hydrate, and treat hypercalcaemia (e.g. with fluids, and where severe, calcitonin or bisphosphonates) under medical supervision.
